note: Numbers a shop or a guide has set. These always win over anything the engine derives. A derived scale is a good default from measured record; a number someone who fishes the water chose is better, and nothing computed may quietly replace it. Add a water here at onboarding and the next scrape keeps what is written rather than overwriting it.

fields.flow.min / flow.max: the scale the bar and sparkline draw against. Derived from USGS daily statistics when absent.
fields.flow.threshold / flow.thresholdLabel: the wading limit. Never derived: this is a person deciding what is safe.
fields.sections: named reaches the pack can be shaped to.
fields.packName: the shop's own name for the pack.
fields.cdecStation: CDEC station id for water temperature (sensor 25, hourly), where USGS does not report 00010. Read through the widget's temp proxy, never from the browser: CDEC sends no CORS header.
fields.reportFreshness: how many days a report stays CURRENT and then RECENT before it reads OLDER, e.g. {"current": 14, "recent": 30}. Never derived. The shop knows how often it updates a water; the card defaults to 14/30 as an INTERIM until they say, and that default is a placeholder, not a standard.

lower-sacramento.why: Chad set this scale and threshold by hand. 7,500 on 0-15,000 puts the wading limit at 50% of the bar, which is why the two-colour split reads as well as it does. The derivation would give 0-30,000 and a limit at 25%.

upper-sacramento.why: Chad set this by hand on 2026-09-07, the same way he set the Lower Sac's 7,500. Never derived: a wading limit is a person deciding what is safe on a river they know. The engine may not compute one, and may not replace one.
